Applicant :- Vijaylaxmi Bindal

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ashish Goyal
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Ajit Madhesia, learned Brief Holder for the State apprised the Court that he has received
instructions in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be
disposed of on merit.
2. Heard Sri Santosh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Ashish Goyal, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Ajit Madhesia, learned Brief Holder for the State.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No.555 of 2023, under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506, 120-B IPC, Police Station-Sadar Bazar, District-Agra, with a prayer to enlarge her on anticipatory bail.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged on 21.10.2023 against the applicant and three others and according to the FIR, applicant executed a sale-deed in favour of the informant in the year 2010 and when in the March, 2023, informant arrived at her plot for construction then one Parmal informed her that the plot in question belongs to him.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of false allegation after 13 years, FIR of the present case was lodged.

He further submits that applicant did not commit any fraud and she rightly sold her property to the informant in the year 2010 and unnecessarily, after 13 years on the basis of false allegation, informant lodged the FIR of the present case.

He further submits that it appears that it is a case of dispute of demarcation of property and when applicant came to know about this fact then she filed a civil suit before the competent court as Suit No.1189 of 2023.

He further submits that applicant is the lady and is not having any criminal history and police is trying to arrest her, therefore, considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, she may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as counsel for the informant however, opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submitted that by playing fraud, applicant duped huge amount of money from the informant and actually applicant was not the owener of the property in question,
but in spite of that she executed sale-deed of the property in favour of the informant and this fact was revealed to the informant in the year 2023 and, thereafter, she lodged the FIR, but both the counsels could not dispute the fact that with regard to the demarcation of the property, a civil suit has been filed by the applicant, which is still pending.
7.
I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Considering the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after more than a decade and prima facie, it appears to be a case of civil dispute and with regard to the demarcation of the property in question a civil suit is pending and applicant is a lady and is not having any criminal history, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
9. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming her independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
